title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

reports.title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

summary:
Matthew and Leah Spurlock were pulled over twice because their Kansas KU Alumni license plate, number 7007, matched a stolen GMC pickup's temporary Kansas tag. Flock cameras in Colwich, Kansas, and later Catoosa, Oklahoma, alerted police to a possible stolen vehicle. In Oklahoma, officers stopped the Spurlocks at gunpoint and handcuffed Matthew before realizing the plate types differed. Kansas uses duplicate numbers across more than 100 plate designs, about half specialty plates, and cameras read only letters and numbers, not backgrounds.

Wichita police Capt. Casey Slaughter said Flock alerts are only a hunch and must be confirmed, but a wrong plate type entered by another agency can still lead to a stop. He said such mistakes are rare. Wichita police have discussed training Flock's AI to recognize plate backgrounds. Kansas is moving from six digit to seven digit, not duplicated plate numbers. The Spurlocks are no longer worried because the stolen vehicle entry has expired, and they hope to keep their 7007 KU plate.
